claim_boundary: replay-free acquisition of an opaque target residual behind a frozen replaceable base with source retention; not general continual learning, universal transfer, or unrestricted computation

baseline_comparison.interpretation: The compact affine source base leaves the target residual learner with a lower-dimensional, better-conditioned source computation than the undertrained nonlinear base at this evidence budget.

controls.fresh_challenger: same target holdout evaluated through the frozen affine base without the target residual
controls.source_retention: source recursive error identical before and after target promotion in all 9 runs
controls.persistence: promoted router round-tripped with the affine base schema intact in all 9 runs

interpretation: This is the first replicated pressure result showing that the factored residual boundary is materially stronger when its shared source computation is an independently replaceable, replay-free affine memory rather than a legacy-shaped nonlinear base. It validates the architecture seam and a bounded capability gain. It does not show that arbitrary new computation can be learned by residual memory, that residual capacity can grow without limit, or that the system has solved general continual learning.
